topics.topic: Layer responsible for detecting duplicate JSON object members before parsing loses them
questions: How is a duplicate object member detected after the JSON text has already been turned into a JSON value, whose ordinary representation cannot retain duplicate members?
Does canonical_bytes receive raw JSON text so it can detect duplicate object keys, or an already parsed JSON value in which duplicate keys can no longer be observed?
Does canonical_bytes receive raw JSON text or an already parsed value, and which layer detects duplicate object keys before parsing loses them?

quotes:
`canonical_bytes` parses JSON text, refuses a duplicate member name,
   a non-finite number and an integer outside ±(2^53 − 1), which an IEEE double
   cannot hold exactly, and emits the JCS form.

canonical_bytes: [BEHAVIOR] MUST parse json_text as one JSON value and emit its RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical form encoded as UTF-8: object members sorted by the UTF-16 code units of their names, numbers written in the ECMAScript shortest round-trip form (an integral double without a fraction or exponent, so a number written 1.0 becomes 1), strings escaped exactly as JCS prescribes, and no whitespace; it applies no Unicode normalization, so two texts that differ only in normalization give different bytes.

canonical_bytes: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise NonCanonicalValueError, with a reason naming the first offending item in text order, when json_text is not one well-formed JSON value, when an object repeats a member name at any depth, when it holds a non-finite number (NaN, Infinity or -Infinity tokens, which the default Python parser would accept and therefore MUST be rejected explicitly), when a number written without a fraction or exponent lies outside plus or minus (2 to the power 53 minus 1), which an IEEE double cannot hold exactly, or when a string holds a lone surrogate.
judgement.why: State 6 makes canonical_bytes consume JSON text and detect repeated member names while parsing it.

topics.topic: Allowed api_base_url components and path-combination rules
questions: Are user information, query, fragment and an existing base path allowed in `api_base_url`, and how are they combined with the declared path?
Are user information, query, fragment, non-root path and trailing slashes allowed in api_base_url, and exactly how are they combined with the declared operation path?

judgement.why: P3 judged the same api_base_url component and path-combination question on the same passages.

precedent.topic: Valid api_base_url components and deterministic joining with operation paths
quotes: prepare_request: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Runs the pre-send checks in exactly this order and returns a PreSendFailure carrying the detail code of the first that fails, with a reason naming it: instance_name is None gives instance_not_selected; base_url is None, or is not an absolute http or https URL with a host, gives instance_address_missing; a plain http target not allowed gives plain_http_not_allowed; two required headers share a name compared without regard to case, or a required header name is in the imported KERNEL_SET_HEADER_NAMES constant without being in the imported INSTANCE_SETTABLE_HEADER_NAMES constant, gives required_header_repeated; a required header whose name is not an HTTP field-name token, or whose value is empty, has leading or trailing whitespace, or holds a control character gives required_header_invalid (= models.DetailCode); then the credential, CredentialUnresolvedError giving credential_unresolved; then input placement, which gives input_not_placeable.

prepare_request: [BEHAVIOR] Builds the URL as base_url without one trailing slash followed by the declared path, each placeholder segment replaced by its input value, which must be a non-null string or an integer written in decimal, UTF-8 percent-encoded except the RFC 3986 unreserved characters so that it stays one segment; nothing else in the URL is normalized.
precedent.why: The later notes accept any absolute HTTP(S) URL with a host, remove exactly one trailing slash, append the declared path, and normalize nothing else.

topics.topic: Allowed multipart port-name characters and escaping or refusal rules

What port-name characters are permitted in multipart names and filenames, and how are quotes, backslashes, controls, non-ASCII characters and CR/LF encoded or refused?

judgement.why: The permitted multipart parameter characters and their escaping or refusal are wire-format and encoding rules belonging to State 6.

judgement.why: Defining the byte or Unicode sequence denoted by a trailing newline is an encoding and input-format rule belonging to State 6.

judgement.why: P1 judged the same startup manifest-validation scope and deterministic capability-failure question on the same texts.

precedent.topic: Startup manifest validation scope and deterministic capability failure order
quotes: read_service_record: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Raises RefusedError naming the first failing check of the record itself, in this order: the record is absent at that revision, is not valid JSON, lacks service or capabilities, its service field differs from service_id, two capabilities share a name.

check_installed_instances: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Takes the services the installation holds a credential for, in service_id order by Unicode code point, and for each raises RefusedError naming that service at the first failure: first the credential header name equals a name in the imported KERNEL_SET_HEADER_NAMES constant compared without regard to case, host included, checked without reading the manifest; then, only when the installation selects an instance for the service, its record read by read_service_record fails any check, or the selected instance named in the record has a required header whose name equals the credential header name compared without regard to case.

check_installed_instances: [BEHAVIOR] A service with no selected instance, or whose record lists no instance of the selected name, fails nothing here; the check reads only the given installation and the manifest, never the store, and returns None when every service passes.
precedent.why: The later notes limit startup validation to credential-bearing services, ordered by service_id, and to top-level service-record checks plus the selected instance's credential-header collision.

topics.topic: Identity fields used to look up a SpooledFile
questions: Is a SpooledFile identified solely by its producing position, or by all M22 meaning facts including digest, size, media type and disclosure class?
Is a SpooledFile’s identity the producer-position tuple alone, or all M22 facts including content and classification?

quotes:
A SpooledFile is named by
its producing position alone (SpooledFileKey); a file already at that position
that no SpooledFile record names — left by a change that failed — is replaced,
and one a record names is never overwritten: that call is `internal_error`.
judgement.why: State 5 explicitly defines the producer-position SpooledFileKey as the lookup identity.

topics.topic: Measurement unit for masked failure-detail length
questions: Is the reported length measured in Unicode scalar values, UTF-8 bytes before truncation, or UTF-8 bytes after truncation?
Is the reported length measured in Unicode code points, UTF-8 bytes, or another unit?

judgement.why: P8 judged the same masked failure-detail length-unit question on the same texts.

precedent.topic: Unit used for masked failure-detail length
quotes: handle_get_repair_view: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] The class of a NodeExecution is the highest class among the items of its inputs, each SpooledFilesRef counting with its disclosure_class even when empty, and when its executed names a binding also of its outputs; the class of an operation execution's failure_detail is the highest of that class and the disclosure classes read_binding declares for that binding's outputs; the class of a TrialExecution is the highest class among its TrialCase's inputs (A07 rule 5, A09 rule 7); a failure_detail becomes DetailLength with its UTF-8 byte length and that class when the reader is an agent and the class is above open, and DetailText otherwise, always for the owner.
precedent.why: The later notes explicitly define the disclosed length as the UTF-8 byte length.

topics.topic: Whether try_implementation returns successful values, digests, or both
questions: Does an explicit try return successful value outputs themselves, only their digests, or both?
Does try_implementation return successful value outputs themselves, or only their digests and comparison result?

judgement.why: P5 judged the same try_implementation successful-output representation question on the same texts.

precedent.topic: Representation of successful outputs in try_implementation responses
quotes: handle_try_implementation: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST call try_implementation with the implementation_id, the trial_case_ids in request order and the actor, and show each returned TrialExecution under the surface masking rule, its outputs through show_port_refs and its failure_detail masked by the class of that execution.

show_port_refs: [FIELD_PROJECTION] For each PortRef, in order, MUST produce one ShownPort with the same port name and one ShownItem per referenced item in order: a StoredValuesRef reads its StoredValue records with read_records using RecordsById, and a value carriage item becomes ShownContent with its value_id, its canonical JSON text read with read_value_bytes from a StoredValueSource and its class, a file carriage item becomes ShownFile with digest, size, media type, class, its value_id and no spooled_file; a SpooledFilesRef reads its SpooledFile records with SpooledFilesByKey and each becomes ShownFile carrying its full SpooledFileKey and no value_id; a FileFactsRef becomes one ShownFile per FileFacts with the class the FileFactsRef carries, no spooled_file and no value_id.

show_port_refs: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] This is the one masking rule of every answer: the owner receives every item in full; when reader is not of kind owner and an item's class is personal_data, MUST produce ShownValueDigest with the value digest and class for a value, or ShownFileDigest with the content digest and class for a file, and read no bytes for it (A07 rule 4).
handle_try_implementation: [RETURN_SHAPE] Returns one ShownTrialExecution per execution, in the order try_implementation returned them.
precedent.why: The later notes require complete shown trial-execution records, resolving non-personal value outputs to canonical JSON content and masking personal-data outputs to digest and class.
